JPM.rationale: JPM presents a strong fundamental picture with clear earnings acceleration and best-in-class franchise quality, but the score is tempered by valuation that is only fair (not cheap) and a near-term reputational overhang. Q1 2026 showed +10% revenue growth and +17.2% EPS growth with expanding operating margins (41.1%) and improving ROE (16.2%). Q2 2026 results (reported 2026-07-14) were even more impressive: $58B revenue (+28% YoY), $21.2B net income (+41% YoY), EPS of $7.70 crushing consensus of $5.55, with every business line posting record revenue. The franchise is structurally dominant (#1 in IB fees 17 years running, $5.1T AUM, 66 countries). Capital return is compelling: 10% dividend increase and $50B buyback after passing stress test with 14.3% Tier 1 ratio. However, PE at 15.8x sits mid-range (13.7-17.8x) — not compellingly cheap given the stock is already 2.3% below its 365-day high at $343.15. P/B at 2.56x is in the upper half of its range. The Epstein allegations targeting CEO Dimon with July 23-24 deadlines for Warren's response and Staley's testimony introduce binary headline risk that caps the near-term upside. The balance sheet has also become more leveraged (assets/equity 13.5x vs 12.4x YoY). On balance, excellent trajectory and franchise quality warrant a solidly positive score, but mid-range valuation and the Epstein overhang prevent a move toward +0.5.
